newsitem.title: USA: Calif governor proposes $2 bln school bond measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif governor proposes $2 bln school bond measure.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Thursday said he would propose a $2 billion statewide school construction bond initiative to be placed on the June 1998 ballot.
Wilson said he would give details of his proposal in his annual State of the State speech next Tuesday.

Wilson also announced that his 1997-98 budget, for the fiscal year starting July 1, would provide $488 million in new funds to extend a class size reduction program to all students in Kindergarten through third grade.

Combined with ongoing funding of $771 million that Wilson said he would commit in his upcoming budget to class-size reduction, total operational funding for the next phase of reducing class sizes would reach $1.259 billion, his office said.

"We should all resolve to do what's best to ensure that every child in California receives the kind of education that prepares them for life's competition," Wilson said in a speech at Frances Willard Elementary School in Long Beach, Calif.
Wilson said his proposed $2 billion bond would help school districts meet the cost of buying new facilities and classrooms needed to make smaller class sizes a reality.

Wilson's office said $1 billion of the bond would be targeted for facilities needs related to class size reduction and the other $1 billion would be earmarked for a new program for growth and modernization.
Wilson said he would also propose "drastic and long overdue reform to the present school construction process."
He called for eliminating "needless costs and overhead" from the current process which he said imposed too many unreasonable costs on communities to get new facilities built and installed.
